Locus Leads on the AFR, EAS and AMR Stores (#405)

Published

November 6, 2026

The question

The EUR sweep (#403) found no (D, W) at which Locus Leads agree with plink2 r² 0.01 clumping closely enough per lead, and its owner’s decision was to judge n_loci_* — a per-Analysis count — by counts: C1 rank, C2 density against HapMap3, C3 cM against bp-only, written into counts.criteria before they were computed. This runs the same sweep on the other ancestries we have a Store and a genotype panel for, each against its own panel and its own map, and answers two predictions of #62’s revision:

  1. Does AFR need a smaller D than EUR? LD decays faster per cM where effective population size is larger, so one cM leaves less LD in AFR.
  2. Is the AMR map usable? Admixture creates long-range LD that LD-based maps read as low recombination, so AMR is the least trustworthy map.

The count criteria below are the ones that judge the count; the per-lead rates stay in as diagnostics, as #403 kept them. Each ancestry was swept one after another, on the same grid and the same 1,000,000-row cap, with seed 405 where the EUR sweep used 403.

The draws

Each draw takes the Analyses a Store assigns that ancestry and measures each one’s Observed Associations at the 5×10⁻⁸ tier. The |z| ≥ 100 and |z| ≥ 38.5 quotas are floors: where the pool has fewer, the draw takes what there is and the record says so (quota_floors). Analyses with no Observed Association at the tier cannot be drawn, and an Analysis whose rows are mostly outside the panel is recorded rather than swept.

Per-lead diagnostics and chance LD

Kept because #403 kept them, and because they say where the two methods disagree. No ancestry’s nearest point meets both tolerances either.

Whether a disagreement straddles a narrow jump in the map is not assessed for these three ancestries: the spike sets #402 found are single populations of the EUR mean map, so the sweeps recorded none (spikes: []). That key means the question was not put to this data, not that no pair straddles anything — the EAS map keeps two such jumps, listed in the map directory’s README.

The nearest (D, W) by the larger of its two rates, its r² 0.01 rates, the bp-only window beside it, and the chance share of its within-Analysis index pairs reaching r² 0.01 — pairs among each Analysis’s clump index variants, so the share moves with how many hits an ancestry has.

Within-Analysis index pairs. Index variants on different chromosomes are unlinked, so the share of such pairs reaching each r² is a chance share — but it is taken among each Analysis’s own clump index variants, so it depends on how many hits that Analysis has. The share is of pairs with a defined r²; EAS’s rests on 92 pairs.

The panel’s own chance LD (ancestries_chance_ld.json): the variant pool is the union of the swept Analyses’ shared sets — the panel as the sweeps used it — and both the variants (at most 3,000 of them) and the cross-chromosome pairs (200,000) are drawn with seed 405. This is a property of the panel’s sample size, not of any Analysis’s hit count.

The two predictions

D is read at the nearest per-lead point and at the point the counts name:

ancestry D at the nearest per-lead point D at the named count point
EUR 0.1 cM bp only / 10 Mb
AFR 0.1 cM none
EAS 0.25 cM 1 cM / 1 Mb
AMR 0.5 cM none

1. Does AFR need a smaller D than EUR? The counts cannot answer it. AFR names no (D, W) at all: C1 holds at 4 of 24 points and C2 at 0, so nothing is named, and both ancestries’ nearest per-lead point is the smallest D the grid holds, 0.1 cM — a measured D for AFR would be at or below the floor, where the grid cannot look. What is observed beside that: at W 1 Mb, rho is 0.975 for AFR at D 0.1 cM and 0.820 with bp only, against 0.997 and 0.993 for EUR, so AFR’s rank agreement is far more sensitive to D than EUR’s, and C3 holds at 4 of 4 W’s for AFR and 0 for EUR. EUR’s own named point is bp only / 10 Mb and its best cM point 2.5 cM at 10 Mb; AFR’s density ratio peaks at 0.760 against EUR’s 0.946 at the same W. That AFR’s counts are more D-sensitive is consistent with the prediction; a smaller calibrated D is not shown, and a grid below 0.1 cM is the owner’s call. - AFR: C1 at 4 of 24 points, C2 at 0, C3 at 4 of 4 W’s. Nearest per-lead point 0.1 cM / 0.25 Mb: 40.4% spurious, 46.7% lost. Within-Analysis index pairs reach r² 0.01 in 1.5% of pairs at 804 samples; the panel’s own chance LD is 1.7%. - EAS: C1 at 24 of 24 points, C2 at 12, C3 at 0 of 4 W’s. Nearest per-lead point 0.25 cM / 0.25 Mb: 15.7% spurious, 15.7% lost. Within-Analysis index pairs reach r² 0.01 in 2.2% of pairs at 817 samples; the panel’s own chance LD is 1.4%. - AMR: C1 at 24 of 24 points, C2 at 0, C3 at 1 of 4 W’s. Nearest per-lead point 0.5 cM / 1 Mb: 33.6% spurious, 39.0% lost. Within-Analysis index pairs reach r² 0.01 in 12.3% of pairs at 345 samples; the panel’s own chance LD is 18.7%. - EUR: C1 at 24 of 24 points, C2 at 20, C3 at 0 of 4 W’s. Nearest per-lead point 0.1 cM / 2.5 Mb: 32.3% spurious, 27.6% lost. Within-Analysis index pairs reach r² 0.01 in 1.2% of pairs at 771 samples; the panel’s own chance LD is 1.2%.

2. Is the AMR map usable? For the count it is as good as any other: C1 holds at 24 of 24 points, and rho runs 0.966 to 0.990. What it cannot do is decide D: C2 fails at every point (the density ratio never reaches 0.8), C3 holds at 1 of 4 W’s, and the ground truth itself is weak here — at 345 samples, 18.7% of unlinked pairs reach r² 0.01 by chance in the panel’s own pool, against 1.7% at 804, 1.4% at 817 and 1.2% at 771. A clump count at r² 0.01 is then partly a chance-LD count, so neither the per-lead rates (33.6% spurious, 39.0% lost) nor a D chosen from it can be trusted. What the splits themselves show is admixture’s long LD: at AMR’s nearest point, 86.0% of its spurious splits lie beyond 1 Mb and 45.7% have r² over 0.05, where chance gives 1.0%; for AFR the two shares are 42.2% and 26.3%, and for EUR 25.9% and 35.1%. No cM distance inside W separates a pair like that. Usable as a rank-preserving count; not usable to calibrate D until there is a ground truth that is not chance LD at that sample size and a rule that sees past W.

What limits the comparison

A drawn Analysis whose rows are mostly absent from its panel is recorded in the sweep’s left_out_below_shared_set_floor and not swept. The floor is 70%; an Analysis just under it loses about a third of its tier rows to variants the panel does not hold.

Reproduce

Each ancestry’s map, selection and sweep, from the repository root:

for a in AFR EAS AMR; do
  pixi run -e dev python -m prototypes.locus_leads build-map \
      --archive /data/opengwasdb/reference/genetic-map/pyrho-1kg-hg38/original/hg38_maps.tar.gz \
      --ancestry $a --output /data/opengwasdb/reference/genetic-map/pyrho-1kg-hg38/$a.tsv.gz
done
pixi run -e dev python -m prototypes.locus_leads select --stores /data/opengwasdb/stores \
    --seed 405 --ancestry AFR --output docs/benchmark-output/locus_leads/ancestries_afr_selection.json
pixi run -e dev python -m prototypes.locus_leads sweep \
    --selection docs/benchmark-output/locus_leads/ancestries_afr_selection.json \
    --stores-dir /data/opengwasdb/stores \
    --genetic-map /data/opengwasdb/reference/genetic-map/pyrho-1kg-hg38/AFR.tsv.gz \
    --panel /data/opengwasdb/reference/hgdp1kgp-hg38/pgen/AFR \
    --hm3 /data/opengwasdb/reference/hapmap3-hg38/hm3.grch38.alid.txt \
    --spikes none --work-dir <scratch directory> \
    --output docs/benchmark-output/locus_leads/ancestries_afr_sweep.json

EAS and AMR repeat the last two commands with their own name, map and panel: EAS uses /data/opengwasdb/reference/hgdp1kgp-hg38/pgen/EAS and AMR /data/opengwasdb/reference/hgdp1kgp-hg38-amr/pgen/AMR. The EUR sweep and its selection are #403’s; eur_sweep.qmd renders them.
